deed: The Bronickis' Ormat, of Yavne, developed a 110-megawatt geothermal power plant in Kenya
title: The Bronickis' Ormat, of Yavne, developed a 110-megawatt geothermal plant in Kenya

trailer.text: Yehuda and Dita Bronicki, winners of the Israel Prize for Industry in 2018, founded Ormat Turbines in 1965.
Yehuda, born in 1934, survived the Holocaust as a child and immigrated to Israel in 1958, and Dita was born in Israel.
In 1998 Ormat won the tender for Olkaria III in Kenya, and developed a 110-megawatt binary geothermal plant there.
According to a Climate Policy Initiative report, it is the first privately funded and developed geothermal project in Africa.

glance.label: Where
glance.value: Olkaria, about 90 km northwest of Nairobi

stations.title: From Poland and Jerusalem to a workshop in Tel Aviv

paragraphs.text: Yehuda Bronicki was born in a region of Poland that is now part of Ukraine.
He was born in 1934 and survived the Holocaust as a child.
He studied for a master's degree in physics at the Sorbonne in Paris, and immigrated to Israel in 1958.
Dita Bronicki was born in Israel and studied at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem.
The two have been married since 1961.
In 1965 the couple sold their apartment in Jerusalem and founded Ormat Turbines.
They acquired a small workshop in Tel Aviv with three employees.
Five years after founding Ormat, the couple opened a vocational high school adjacent to the factory in Yavne, and it still operates under the auspices of the ORT network.
According to the CPI report, in 2010–2014 nearly 80% of Kenya's residents lived without electricity.
Kenya was highly dependent on electricity from hydropower plants, which was not reliable.
According to the report, as of March hydroelectric power plants made up almost 50% of installed capacity, and they caused several power outages.
According to the report, the heat in the ground there was developed very slowly, because the private sector barely took part.
According to MIGA, the severe power shortage hampered Kenya's economic growth.
The Olkaria geothermal fields lie in the Rift Valley, about 90 km northwest of Nairobi.

stations.title: The tender and the first phase

paragraphs.text: In 1998 Ormat was declared the winner of the Olkaria III concession tender.
The government had already explored the resources at the site before Ormat developed it.
KenGen provided data on the resource and donated 8 megawatts of wells to Ormat.
According to the report, the plant has 22 production wells.
14 of them were drilled in the first phase, and two of these were donated by KenGen.
8 more wells were drilled in the second and third phases.
The first phase, of about 13 megawatts, began operating.
Two sources differ on when it began operating.
According to Renewable Energy World, the second phase, of about 35 megawatts, began commercial operation in January 2009.
According to Globes, after this expansion the plant was a 48-megawatt power plant.
In 2010 Ormat's subsidiary signed a letter of intent with Kenya's power company, KPLC, to expand the plant.
The plan was to add up to 52 megawatts, from 48 to up to 100 megawatts.
Dita Bronicki said at the time that Kenya is a proven and significant resource for geothermal energy.
She said the expansion would provide Kenya with renewable, dependable and cost-effective electricity.
In 2013 Ormat began commercial operation of Plant 2 at Olkaria, adding 36 megawatts.
Ormat's total capacity worldwide then reached 611 megawatts.
According to Power Engineering, Ormat planned a third unit of 16 megawatts, expected to be completed in 2014.
According to the CPI report, the plant reached 110 megawatts and full commercial operation in February 2014.
That month, Dita Bronicki was serving as CEO of Ormat.
According to her, Olkaria III is a prime example of multi-stage development, which generates higher returns and reduces risk.
She also said that Ormat had achieved the growth ahead of schedule, and that this led to a significant increase in revenues.
According to the report, working phase by phase allowed the reservoir to be exploited progressively.
The plant reached full capacity within 16 years.
According to ThinkGeoEnergy, Ormat itself financed both phases of the project and the well drilling, from internal funds.
According to the CPI report, the project cost $445 million.
Kenya's Vice President said at the inauguration ceremony that the $150 million invested by Ormat is the largest single private investment in the power sector.
Later, loan financing also came.
In November 2013 Ormat drew down the remaining $45 million under the financing facility, to complete Plant 3.
According to the report, debt from development institutions now accounts for 85% of overall investment costs.
The subsidiary OrPower 4, wholly owned by Ormat, closed a financing agreement for a plant in Naivasha, Kenya.
On September 22, 2011, MIGA issued a $99 million guarantee for Ormat's equity investment in OrPower 4.
The amount of financing for Plant 4 was not disclosed, but the company said it came from equity.
According to Globes, in 2009 the project supplied 6% of Kenya's total energy production.
Kenya's Vice President said the green technology at the plant would help reduce the cost of electricity.
According to him, it will save the country 120 thousand tons of imported oil.
The electricity is sold under a 20-year agreement with Kenya's power company, KPLC.
Ormat CEO Isaac Angel said that the complex will supply clean and reliable electricity to more than 250 thousand households in Kenya.
According to the Daily Nation, Ormat added another 29 megawatts at the Olkaria station.
According to the report, the cost of electricity at Olkaria III is 13% lower than the average for similar geothermal projects in Kenya.
According to CPI's estimate, the internal rate of return on equity is 16% after tax.
According to the report (2015), this is the only geothermal project operating in Kenya so far with private participation from field development through to operation and maintenance.
Non-condensable gases generated yearly as a by-product of geothermal resource extraction are sometimes piped to a neighboring farm for use in a greenhouse.
Gases generated as a by-product of extracting the heat are sometimes piped to a neighboring farm, for use in a greenhouse.

stations.title: The people and the company today

paragraphs.text: Yehuda and Dita managed Ormat and its subsidiaries for 50 years, from its founding until 2014.
In 2018 the couple were awarded the Israel Prize for Industry.
The couple are no longer at the helm of Ormat, and the company is still flourishing.
When the second phase of Olkaria III (48 megawatts) was completed, Lucien Bronicki was Chairman and Chief Technical Officer of Ormat, based in Yavne.
Ormat Technologies is listed on the New York Stock Exchange and operates Olkaria III.
At the end of 2025 Ormat employed 1,648 people, and according to the Weizmann Institute its equipment produces clean energy in 30 countries.
The company said Kenya is an important market for its growth, because of its high geothermal potential.
It said it is focusing on increasing its operations there.
In the early 1970s the company had difficulty operating its turbines in Alaska, because the liquid in them froze in the extreme cold.
In Kenya, too, the road was long.
Ormat had to invest its own equity for longer than expected, and managed to obtain loans only 11 years from the start of the project.
Lengthy negotiations over the electricity price led to the amendment of the prior agreements and the restatement of the agreement in 2007.
According to the report, when private investors are attracted even before exploration drilling, governments may have to offer a higher electricity price, because of the risks.

claims.text: ב-1965 מכרו בני הזוג את דירתם בירושלים, הקימו את אורמט טורבינות ורכשו בתל אביב סדנה קטנה עם שלושה עובדים.
claims.quote: In 1965, they sold their apartment in Jerusalem and set up Ormat Turbines Ltd. (later Ormat Industries) and acquired a small workshop in Tel Aviv with three employees.

claims.text: בני הזוג זכו בפרס ישראל לתעשייה ב-2018.
claims.quote: the same year they were awarded the Israel Prize for Industry

claims.text: יהודה ברוניצקי שרד את השואה כנער צעיר.
claims.quote: There, as a young teen, he survived the Holocaust.

claims.quote: an MSc in physics at the Sorbonne in Paris, he immigrated to Israel in 1958.

claims.text: דיטה ברוניצקי נולדה בישראל ולמדה באוניברסיטה העברית בירושלים; בני הזוג נשואים מאז 1961.
claims.quote: Dita was born in Israel and studied at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem. They have been married since 1961.

claims.text: מכרז הקונסיון של אולקריה III נקבע לאורמט ב-1998.
claims.quote: which was awarded to Ormat Technologies in 1998

claims.quote: Olkaria III is a 110 MW binary geothermal power plant, whose resources were explored by the government before development was undertaken by private actor Ormat Technologies.

claims.text: לפי דוח של Climate Policy Initiative, אולקריה III היא הפרויקט הגיאותרמי הראשון באפריקה שמומן ופותח באופן פרטי.
claims.quote: The Olkaria III project is the first privately funded and developed geothermal project in Africa.

claims.text: החשמל מאולקריה III נמכר במסגרת הסכם רכישת חשמל ל-20 שנה עם חברת החשמל של קניה (KPLC).
claims.quote: is sold under a 20-year power purchase agreement (PPA) with Kenya Power and Lighting Company Limited (KPLC).

claims.text: מנכ"ל אורמט יצחק אנג'ל אמר שמתחם אולקריה III יספק חשמל נקי ואמין ליותר מ-250 אלף משקי בית בקניה.
claims.quote: the Olkaria III complex will provide clean and reliable electricity to over 250,000 households in Kenya

claims.text: לוסיאן ברוניצקי הוא יושב ראש ומנהל טכנולוגי ראשי של אורמט, שמושבה ביבנה, ישראל.
claims.quote: said Lucien Bronicki, Chairman and Chief Technical Officer of Yavne, Israel-based Ormat.

claims.text: התחנה נמצאת בשדות הגיאותרמיים של אולקריה בבקע הסורי-אפריקאי, כ-90 ק"מ צפון-מערבית לנאירובי.
claims.quote: The project involves the expansion of a base-load geothermal power plant in the Olkaria geothermal fields of the Rift Valley, 90 kilometers northwest of Nairobi.

claims.text: יהודה ברוניצקי נולד באזור בפולין שהיום הוא חלק מאוקראינה.
claims.quote: Yehuda Bronicki was born in a region of Poland that is now part of Ukraine.

claims.text: חמש שנים לאחר הקמת אורמט פתחו בני הזוג בית ספר תיכון מקצועי סמוך למפעל ביבנה, שעדיין פועל בחסות רשת אורט.
claims.quote: the Bronickis opened a vocational high school adjacent to the factory in Yavne that still operates under the auspices of the ORT network of trade schools.

claims.quote: 22 production wells: 14 in Phase I (2 of which donated by KenGen, for a total of 8MW), 8 in Phase II and III

claims.quote: The first phase of approximately 13 MW commenced commercial operations in August 2000 and the second phase of approximately 35 MW commenced operation in January 2009.

claims.text: ב-2013 החלה אורמט הפעלה מסחרית בתחנה 2 באולקריה, והוסיפה 36 מגהוואט לקיבולת הכוללת שלה, שהגיעה ל-611 מגהוואט ברחבי העולם.

claims.text: בראשית שנות ה-70 התקשתה אורמט להפעיל את הטורבינות שלה באלסקה, כי הנוזל בהן קפא בקור הקיצוני.
claims.quote: Ormat was having technical difficulties operating its turbines in Alaska because the liquid in the turbines would freeze in the extreme cold.

claims.text: אורמט נאלצה להאריך את מחויבות ההון העצמי שלה מעבר לצפוי ואבטחה חוב רק 11 שנים מתחילת הפרויקט.
claims.quote: Ormat had to extend its equity commitment for longer than originally expected, securing debt financing only 11 years from the inception of the project.

claims.text: משא ומתן ממושך על תעריף ההסכם הוביל לתיקון ההסכמים הקודמים ולניסוח מחדש של ההסכם ב-2007.
claims.quote: The lengthy negotiation on the PPA tariff resulted in the amendment of the prior agreements and the restatement of the PPA in 2007

claims.text: לפי הדוח, משיכת השקעה פרטית לפני קידוחי חקר עשויה לחייב ממשלות להציע תעריף גבוה יותר בשל הסיכונים.
claims.quote: attracting private investment in project development before exploration drilling could require governments to offer a higher tariff because of the risks

claims.text: לפי הדוח, אורמט הלוותה הון עצמי: התחייבות ראשונית של 40 מיליון דולר ב-1998–1999 שהגיעה ל-150 מיליון דולר ב-2006.
claims.quote: The private developer Ormat provided equity financing with an initial USD 40 million commitment in the years 1998-1999, which reached USD 150 million in 2006.

claims.text: בטבלת המימון של CPI מופיעה תרומת ההון העצמי של אורמט בשלבים השונים בסך כולל של 220 מיליון דולר.
claims.quote: Ormat Technologies Equity Private 40 110 43 27 220

claims.text: לפי NS Energy (2014), עם כניסת תחנה 3 לפעילות הקיבולת הכוללת של המתחם עלתה ל-110 מגהוואט.
claims.quote: total generation capacity has increased to 110 MW.

claims.text: לפי Power Engineering (2013), התחנה השלישית אמורה להעלות את הקיבולת הכוללת של הפרויקט ל-100 מגהוואט.
claims.quote: The third plant will bring the project’s total generating capacity up to 100 MW.

claims.text: לפי Daily Nation, הקיבולת החדשה מביאה את סך התפוקה של מפעלי החברה ל-139 מגהוואט.
claims.quote: The new capacity brings the total output from the firm’s plants to 139 megawatts.

claims.text: לפי דוח CPI, אורמט הכריזה על הרחבה נוספת של 24 מגהוואט במתחם אולקריה, שצפויה לעלות לרשת במחצית השנייה של 2016.
claims.quote: Ormat has also announced an additional 24 MW expansion of the Olkaria complex, expected to come on line in the second half of 2016
